Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Deuteronomy (c. 365 AD)

On the Song of Moses' line 'when the Most High divided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the sons of God' (Deu 32:8, LXX / Dead Sea Scrolls reading 'sons of God' / b'nei Elohim — preserved in the Masoretic-correction tradition), Ephrem reads the verse as the canonical Old-Testament anchor of the doctrine of angelic-territorial-governance: the Most High assigned each nation to the oversight of an angelic prince, retaining Israel as his own portion (Deu 32:9). Tewahedo angelology preserves this doctrine prominently — the Synaxarium accounts of Saint Michael as guardian-prince of Ethiopia, the Tewahedo Mäshafä Hēnok (1 Enoch) traditions of the seventy shepherds (1 En 89-90), and the Mäṣḥafä Kufāle (Jubilees) accounts of the angel-of-the-presence assigned to Israel (Jub 1:27, 2:1, 15:31-32) all flow from Deu 32:8's canonical seed. Tewahedo cites Deu 32:8 + Jub 15:31-32 + 1 En 89:59 as the canonical triple-witness of angelic-territorial-governance.
